diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/6 is down, affecting all 29 customers assigned to that PON port. The OLT itself is healthy and responsive; the healthy overall status is a monitoring defect that concealed the failed port.
evidence: The subscriber has a definite offline result: SNMP responds, online is 0, and the ONU reports MPCP DEREG.
All seven tested ONUs on EPON0/6 are definite negatives, so this is not a single-ONU fault or a monitoring timeout.
The port has 29 customers and the trigger reports 29 offline customers, matching the full port population.
The other seven PON ports are healthy, while OLT ping, SNMP, metrics, and uptime are normal; therefore this is not an OLT-wide or router failure.
Because the entire affected port is down, the correct fault type is pon_port_failure rather than splitter_failure.

Historical optical telemetry was stable around RX -20 dBm, TX +2.3 dBm, constant distance, and healthy bias current; the final null readings are a consequence of the outage, not evidence of fibre or laser degradation.
The VLAN is correctly provisioned and RADIUS is consistent, with only one normal session in the last 24 hours, so authentication and VLAN faults are excluded.
The OLT overall_status of healthy contradicts the failed-port detail and conceals a genuine minority-port outage; the service fault remains the PON port failure.

remediation.action: Escalate to PON access maintenance. Check EPON0/6 for port, line-card, optic, and configuration faults; reset or replace the port/optic as appropriate, then verify ONU registration and traffic for all 29 customers. Correct the OLT health check so a failed PON is reported despite other healthy ports.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/6 has failed, taking 28 of its 29 customers offline simultaneously 80 minutes ago. The twenty-ninth ONU had already been offline for three days from an unrelated individual fault and is not part of this event.
expected_reasoning: Every ONU on EPON0/6 now returns responds true with online 0
28 of the 29 stopped within the same minute, 80 minutes ago
One ONU on the port last held a session three days ago, so it was already down before this event
That ONU's separate history excludes it from this incident's affected set
OLT ping and SNMP succeed and the other seven ports are serving normally
The failure boundary follows EPON0/6 exactly
PON port traffic has collapsed from 231 Mbps average to 8 Mbps
distractors: The trigger states 29 offline, inviting that number to be reported as the blast radius
All 29 look identical in current state and only history separates them
